scope: Audit which broad Wild Hearthstone mechanics can already map into the current HSConfig normal-path runtime surfaces without blocking package generation, which can only map partially through generic timing or target posture, and which should remain warning-only because the actual game decision surface is still outside the documented HSConfig and VisionAI no-block contract.
source_backed_facts: The current HSConfig normal path is still centered on GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, per-card <CardID>.json runtime files, and exact Combo.json only when ordered combo rows exist.

The documented claim kinds and card-behavior registry already support discover_choice, choose_one_choice, hero_power_transform, targeted Battlecry behavior, attack posture, and other concrete per-card behaviors when source evidence and identity links are strong enough.
Battlecry is direct enough for normal-path lowering because BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus already exists as a documented runtime block and current HSConfig code paths already use it.

Discover is direct enough for normal-path lowering because OnDiscoverCardBonus is documented and current router behavior already lowers exact Discover option identities when source evidence resolves the option card.

Choose One is direct enough for normal-path lowering because OnChooseOneCardBonus is a documented supported block in the local registry and current router and prepare tests already prove exact choose_one_choice lowering when option identity is resolved.

Transformed Hero Powers are direct enough for normal-path lowering because hero_power_transform is a supported claim kind and BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus is already part of the normal card-behavior registry.

Weapons are direct enough for normal-path lowering because current code already maps weapon and hero-attack posture into BeforePhysicalAttackBonus and existing Wild fixture families already cover weapon pressure.

Overload is direct enough for normal-path lowering because it is already mapped into BeforePlayCardBonus as a timing-family mechanic, even though future-mana optimisation remains heuristic rather than explicit.

Discard is direct enough for normal-path lowering because current router tests already prove discard mechanic_usage can lower through documented explicit runtime blocks, and the Discolock fixture family already validates the general runtime lane.
Deathrattle is only partial because current HSConfig can express play timing or on-board value, but it still has no first-class deathrattle trigger planner or resurrection-quality surface.

Recruit and summon-from-deck effects are only partial because HSConfig can time the recruiter but cannot directly control which exact card is pulled beyond deck construction and source-backed sequence context.

Freeze is only partial because battlecry-based or hero-power-based freeze can map to documented target surfaces, but generic spell-target freeze still lacks a dedicated normal-path spell-target block.
Lifesteal is only partial because current surfaces can prefer playing or attacking with the card, but heal-threshold planning and stabilisation logic are not first-class mechanic blocks.
Rush, Charge, and Taunt are only partial as a group because Rush and Charge fit attack posture well, while Taunt is mostly indirect board-value posture with no dedicated taunt-specific runtime block.

Locations are only partial because the current compiler recognizes them as a card family, but the normal no-block runtime path still treats them mostly as generic play-timing cards rather than repeated-use board objects.

Secrets are only partial because current surfaces can lower the decision to play the secret, but secret ordering, hidden-information timing traps, and layered secret interaction remain outside first-class runtime lowering.
Generated entities are only partial because deterministic linked entities can lower safely, while random creation pools, unstable token identities, and unresolved option trees must stay suppressed.
Aura and ongoing effects are only partial because HSConfig can value playing or preserving the aura source, but it cannot compute the full downstream board-state math as a dedicated runtime family.

Destroy is only partial because battlecry-based or attack-based destroy can map into existing target or attack posture surfaces, while generic spell-target destroy still lacks a direct normal-path target block.
Silence is only partial because battlecry-based or timing-based silence can lower, but generic silence-spell target selection is still outside the documented runtime contract.

Transform is only partial because battlecry-based transform and some untargeted timing rules can lower, but generic spell-based transform target choice and random transform outcomes are not first-class normal-path surfaces.

Dredge should remain warning-only in the current no-block contract because the real bottom-three choice semantics are not a documented first-class runtime surface, even though the current router can reuse a discover-like fallback role.
Tradeable should remain warning-only because timing the card or reflecting mulligan posture is not the same as lowering the actual trade action as a runtime behavior.

Board-position effects should remain warning-only because the current card-behavior registry exposes no documented normal-path block for left-right placement, adjacency preservation, or slot-sensitive summon positioning.

Current Wild stress examples outside the older core fixture mix include Secret Mage, Questline Mage, XL Mage, Overload Shaman, Kingsbane Rogue, Highlander Priest, XL Shadow Priest, and Treant Druid, which together cover secrets, discover, freeze, location pressure, choose-one usage, weapons, and transformed hero-power pressure.
no_block_implications: The no-block promise should continue to mean that every valid deck can produce a structurally load-safe package even when some mechanics only lower partially or remain warning-only.

Direct mechanic groups such as Battlecry, Discover, Choose One, Weapons, Overload, Discard, and Transformed Hero Powers can produce real normal-path runtime rows today when the source contract is sufficiently resolved.

Partial mechanic groups should continue to emit runtime rows only for the parts that map cleanly to documented blocks, while the unresolved parts stay visible in suppression reports, readiness reports, or warning summaries rather than blocking apply.

Warning-only mechanic groups such as Dredge, Tradeable, and board-position effects should stay explicitly visible as uncovered or warning-boundary semantics instead of being promoted into invented runtime JSON.
This boundary preserves honest load safety: technically valid packages still apply, while unsupported mechanic detail remains visible and non-blocking rather than being silently hidden.

The no-block contract does not justify weaker technical validation. Invalid JSON, unsupported runtime files or blocks, malformed Mulligan or Combo rows, and GameCardId or profile drift must still hard-block as before.
mechanic_or_surface_gaps: Generic spell-target mechanics are still the biggest gap in the current no-block normal path. Discover, Choose One, Battlecry targets, Hero Powers, and physical attack posture have documented surfaces; generic spell targets still do not.
Dredge remains an over-claim risk because a discover-like fallback is not the same thing as a true first-class Dredge choice surface.
Tradeable remains an over-claim risk because play timing and mulligan treatment do not express the actual trade action.
Board-position effects remain fully outside the current documented runtime contract. There is still no first-class place-left, place-right, preserve-adjacency, or slot-priority block.
Locations remain under-surfaced because the normal path recognizes the card family but not the repeated-use location activation lifecycle as a dedicated runtime mechanic.
Generated entities remain mixed because deterministic linked outputs are safe, while random generated branches or unresolved identities would become fabricated behavior if lowered too aggressively.

Because the representative fixture set is finite, future Wild deck combinations can still land in generic-low-confidence, source-informed, or warning-only lanes without contradicting the no-block promise.
implementation_pressure: No broad runtime-surface expansion is justified by the current evidence. The higher-value near-term pressure is narrow and test-oriented: preserve the direct lanes that already exist, keep partial and warning-only mechanic boundaries explicit in docs and reports, and only widen the representative fixture set when a specific currently unsupported Wild family needs stronger proof.
confidence: high: the current HSConfig operator docs, local card-behavior policy, router code, compiler code, registry, fixture tests, and current Wild mechanic references all support the same direct-versus-partial-versus-warning-only boundary for a no-block package contract.
